THAT REMEDY IS WRONG AND IMPLEMENTING IT WOULD HAVE CONTRADICTED AN hv RULING. cc classified every UNACCOUNTED path against data-model.md's own "What is deliberately not modelled" section rather than against their assumption, and found FIVE classes under one word: baize 135 = whiteboard 110 / declared-out-of-model 14 / generated projections 6 / config 3 / placeholders 2; canary 347 = 97 / 226 / 21 / 1 / 2. THE LARGEST CLASS IS MODELLED, NOT OUT OF MODEL. data-model.md:510 reads, verbatim: "The whiteboard LEFT this set at D30 (hv ruling, 2026-08-15) and is modelled above as wb_node/wb_item/wb_message, built in WP-14." So those 110 files are MODELLED AND UNBUILT, and declaring them out-of-model would be the denominator attack that sync.rs warns about in its own words -- a set this code chose for itself would be a denominator certifying itself; naming everything zeroes the loss. cc was about to implement exactly that while quoting the warning, and was stopped only by pinning the set to the authorising document. THE CORRECTED BLOCKER, IN cc's WORDS: the migrator does not say WHAT IT DID NOT CARRY, and the largest unnamed class is one the model CLAIMS. The remedy is three parts, ruled 2026-08-31: (1) the migrator names what it did not carry IN CLASSES, each pinned to its authorising sentence in the NOT_CARRIED shape (shown + justified_by), with a test that reds when the document stops carrying the phrase -- the test is load-bearing, because a citation without it is a copy and a copy of a ruling goes stale the day the ruling moves; (2) the whiteboard class is named as a WP-14 GAP, never as out-of-model -- the model claims these and the migrator does not yet carry them, nothing is destroyed, and a gap that expires when WP-14 lands is worth more than a zero that never does; (3) conservation_check.sh splits UNACCOUNTED into the five classes -- ic's tool, cc's census -- because a token spanning the acceptable and the unacceptable case cannot discriminate, which is the same defect as `named` conflating the check finding a residue with the MIGRATION naming it. THIS IS THE SECOND INSTANCE IN ONE SESSION OF THE MISSING `issues edit` PREVENTING A CORRECTION, both times in the record of a finding about the very thing hv's unexecuted write-path ruling would have fixed.
